tweets.text:
Should you be on Reddit to drive LLM recommendations?

One of Discuss GTM’s chat members shared an unreviewed preprint study I just finished reading. It looks at whether Reddit shapes which brands AI tools recommend – even when the tools don’t cite Reddit.

Sample and methodology:

The author pulled 12K posts and 100K+ comments from 60 subreddits via Reddit’s API.

Brand mentions were scored by upvotes, placement (title, body, comment), and comment depth.

Those scores were then ranked against brand recommendations from ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and Gemini across 50 product queries, each asked three times. The correlation analysis spans 12 consumer categories.

A second test compared Reddit citations in 60 API calls (15 queries) vs. 100 web UI queries per platform, collected via browser automation in February 2026.

Key findings:

• Reddit brand rankings and AI brand rankings lined up fairly strongly.
• Web UIs cited Reddit in 44% of queries on Google AI Mode, 20% on Perplexity, and 17% on ChatGPT.
• APIs returned 0% Reddit citations on every platform.
• Opinion and comparison queries pulled in Reddit most often: 70.8% on Google AI Mode and 45.8% on Perplexity.
• Claude cited Reddit zero times in both channels, but it cited any source in only 19% of web UI queries.

Now, how I read it.

Reddit may influence LLM recommendations even when it’s not cited.

The big implication: citation tracking alone may underestimate Reddit’s role. If brand rankings on Reddit correlate with brand recommendations from LLMs, Reddit may function as a background reputation / consensus layer – not just a direct source.

Remember my post about fan-out queries? Here’s the answer for getting into an LLM’s pre-search association brain.

So “being cited” and “shaping the answer” are two different things.

Reddit also seems especially relevant for high-consideration / opinion-heavy queries. So if you’re in a very competitive field and switching costs are high—yeah, you have to think about building a presence on Reddit.

Shilling is also not the answer.

Engagement quality > raw mention volume.

Because the Reddit score included upvotes, title/body placement, and comment depth, the implied signal is a brand showing up in substantive, highly engaged discussions.

Reddit = reputation channel.

I definitely need to research more guerrilla tactics on Reddit. For now, I’m just passively growing karma—but I’m not sure how to inject brand discussions without it becoming shilling / spam.

Feel free to share your ideas.

PS: This study is an unreviewed preprint from a consultancy with a stake in GEO advice, and it’s co-written with Claude folks.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — OCTOBER 28, 2026

Fed day. Rising oil, a firm dollar and 10-year Treasury yields around 5% are keeping metals investors on edge.

⚛️ URANIUM
The latest weekly report puts spot at $89.85/lb, while October’s long-term price rose to $97. Reported term contracting has reached 80.4M lbs this year versus 47.9M at the same point last year. Utilities are getting busier. Contract prices deserve more attention than a quiet spot market.

🥈 SILVER
Back around $53.82 in early trading, down roughly 1%. Yesterday’s rebound is already being tested. A hawkish Fed message could keep pressure on a metal caught between investment demand and growth concerns.

🔶 COPPER
LME three-month copper traded at $14,430/t yesterday. China’s Yangshan import premium hit $188/t, its highest in nearly 13 years. Physical demand is providing support even as the dollar pushes back.

🥇 GOLD
Around $4,030 early today, down 0.7%. Oil’s renewed rise is reviving inflation fears and expectations that rates stay elevated.

👀 TODAY’S WATCH
A Fed hold is widely expected. The bigger question is what policymakers signal about December.
My take: rates dominate precious metals for now, while copper’s import premiums and uranium’s term market show why each metal needs its own supply-and-demand analysis.

This article is full of blatant misinformation.  

"The components Luckey specified that are planned to be American-made from the start are the display glass, the frame around the display, and parts of the ribbon component." 

No.  That is not what I said.  This was a response to a specific question about the display modules in the current prototype vs the final product.  As I explicitly said, BlueChip has American chips, batteries, metallics, plastics, glass, etc, and we have a clear technical roadmap to 100% American components. 

"It sounds like BlueChip’s first laptop will be well below the 65-percent requirement to count as American-made" 

This is nuts.  There is a reason no other reporter has came to this conclusion.  One hint might be the extended discussion we had explicitly about the government requirements for American-made hardware and why meeting that bar is so important.

"Palmer Luckey is of course a controversial figure, with his history of fueling right wing troll farms" 

This never happened.  You are pushing a lie The Verge has pushed for over a decade now.  Yes, you have written a bunch of stories claiming this happened, but it just ain't so.  I gave $9,000 to a group that ran a single anti-Clinton billboard.  The "right wing troll farms" narrative was a fabricated story pushed shortly before the 2016 election because Dems desperately wanted a right-wing equivalent to the actually-real Correct The Record, an online astroturfing organization that paid people to troll and "correct" Trump supporters online.  

But there was no such thing.  It was all disinformation.  Which is why most of the stories about it were later deleted.  Yet here you are, lying again.
